Subject: SOC2 ask: one-page diagram + decision log for Dedicated vs Private topologies

Hi Marcus / Kimberly / Marissa,

BluePeak is kicking off the SOC 2 readiness review for Redwood. For the CAIQ/SIG mapping we need a concise artifact describing the network/isolation model for your Dedicated and Private offerings. Specifically: 

- A single-page diagram per topology (visual) showing control-plane/data-plane separation, KMS boundaries, egress paths, and any customer-managed networking points.
- A short decision log (CSV or table) that captures why certain isolation choices were made (e.g., shared control plane vs private control plane, tenant overlays vs separate GPU pools), who approved the choice, and references to design docs.

Can you provide both by end of day Thursday (2027-07-22)? If a short runbook (2–3 pages) that covers operator steps to verify isolation quickly is available, please include that as well — that helps us map controls to SOC 2 criteria and answer CAIQ sections.

A few SCQs up front: Do you offer an air-gapped option for Private? Is hardware-level separation available for Dedicated customers who request it?

Thanks,
Amelia Bryant
Senior Auditor, BluePeak Security
amelia@bluepeak.io

Kimberly / Ben / Marissa: can you take the lead on artifacts? My plan:
- Kimberly: produce the one-page diagrams (Dedicated.pdf and Private.pdf). Focus on control/data plane surfaces, KMS boundaries, and egress/ingress choke points.
- Ben: provide the decision log CSV capturing rationale, owners, and links to longer design docs.

Dedicated is hosted in our dedicated GPU pools; for customers with strict separation needs we offer reserved hardware pools and can isolate at the NIC/tenant overlay level — hardware-level physical separation is available as an add-on (procurement lead required).

I'll target an initial drop by tomorrow EOD for the diagrams and the decision log draft the next day.

Notes (summary):
- Private (customer-hosted / on-prem): customer-provided VPC or physical network. Control plane can be run as a private control plane (customer-managed URL or privately-peered control endpoint). Data plane is entirely within the customer's network. KMS integration is via customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed key in a customer VPC/HSM. Egress: by default no shared egress; outbound internet controlled by customer NAC. Air-gap: supported for on-prem installs (installation runbook exists).

- Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools are logically isolated tenant pools inside Redwood's cloud regions. We provide a tenant overlay (VLAN/NIC) per customer; control plane remains in Redwood-managed control-plane but segregated logically and can be region-specific. KMS: Redwood-managed KMS with customer CMK option in some providers. Egress: egress policies enforced at the host-level and by network ACLs; default path is via Redwood transit but can be routed to customer-provided egress (via peering) for enterprise contracts.

Decision highlights (in CSV):
- Chosen isolation model for Dedicated: logical isolation + tenant overlay + optional reserved hardware pools (reason: predictable throughput + cost efficiency; approved by infra and legal).
- Chosen isolation model for Private: physical / network isolation with optional private control plane (reason: regulatory isolation; approved by SOC/Legal).

I'll add callouts on the diagram for KV cache boundaries and smart routing fallback (e.g., can route to smaller models in a different pool if capacity constrained).

Ben — can you confirm the approval lines and update the 'approved_by' column?

3) Hardware separation: the decision log notes 'optional reserved hardware pools' — does that map to physically dedicated GPUs on separate hosts, or just dedicated tenant scheduling on shared racks? We need the exact wording.

Amelia — thanks for the follow-ups. Delivering the concise artifacts below and answers inline. All items uploaded to the link in the header.

Attachments (inline):
- 20270720-dedicated-private-onepager.pdf (visuals)
- 20270721-isolation-decision-log.csv (rationale + approved_by)
- 20270722-compact-runbook.md (operator verification checklist)

Short answers: 
1) Control plane for Dedicated: the control plane is Redwood-managed and does accept tenant metadata (routing, model version pins, telemetry IDs) but we do not persist customer secrets in the control plane. Any sensitive keys (KMS material) are either stored in customer KMS (Private deployments) or in Redwood KMS with strict access policies and KMS audits (Dedicated). Control-plane compute is multi-tenant logical infrastructure but access controls and RBAC prevent cross-tenant secret exposure. We have additional hardened paths for enterprise customers that require a private control plane (see diagram note "private-control-plane option").

2) Operator verification steps (excerpt from compact-runbook.md):
- Verify network namespace isolation: run 'ip netns' / check tenant overlay assignments and confirm no external routes in the tenant VPC.
- Confirm KMS bindings: validate CMK presence and rotation records (show last rotation timestamp).
- Egress validation: trigger a test call and inspect egress route in VPC flow logs; confirm outbound CIDR-to-IP mapping matches expected peer.
- Control plane audit: query control-plane audit logs for the time window and confirm only RBAC-allowed principals performed sensitive operations.
(Full CSV of checks included in the runbook and the operator checklist file).

3) Hardware separation: reserved hardware pools map to physically isolated hosts in the cloud provider when selected. We offer two modes: 
- Logical reserved pools (dedicated scheduling and tenant overlays on shared racks) — the default for cost/throughput tradeoff.
- Physical host isolation (physical GPU segregation on distinct hosts with no shared NICs by guest tenants) — available as a paid add-on for higher assurance customers. The decision log column 'hardware_isolation' spells out which customers opted for which mode.

If BluePeak needs an export of the host mapping and procurement ticket for customers that have chosen physical isolation, we can produce a redacted inventory under a separate NDA.

Let us know if anything else is required; otherwise we consider the CAIQ/SIG items addressed for these sections.

Thanks — Marcus
